title: Near-real-time monitoring of global ocean carbon sink

en.text: The ocean is one of the planet's largest buffers against climate change, soaking up roughly a quarter of the carbon dioxide humanity emits every year. Yet our best official accounting of how much it absorbs, the annual Global Carbon Budget, always trails reality by about a year. When the ocean's uptake shifts, we cannot see it until long after the fact.

That lag is not an oversight; it is built into how the number is produced. The ocean biogeochemical models (GOBMs) that estimate the sink are computationally heavy, and the surface-ocean CO2 observations that data-driven products depend on are themselves delayed by roughly a year. So the community has detailed, trustworthy databases of ocean carbon fluxes that are always looking backward in time.

This is an awkward gap at exactly the wrong moment. As countries move through the global stocktake under the Paris Agreement, they need to know where the carbon is going now, not a year ago. The paper's contribution is a way to close that gap: Carbon Monitor Ocean, or CMO-NRT, a near-real-time, monthly, gridded dataset of global surface-ocean CO2 fugacity (fCO2) and air-sea CO2 flux, together with the deep-learning framework that produces it.
Links
Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.01637
Code: https://github.com/kepiyu/CMO-NRT
Dataset (Figshare): https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.24658494.v1 | Live project: https://carbonsink.microsoft.com/

The key design choice is what CMO-NRT does not do: it does not try to replace the trusted community models. Instead it learns to reproduce them from inputs that are available in near-real-time. Each GOBM or data product becomes a target that a neural network learns to predict from observable quantities, so that once those observables arrive for the current month, the model can extend the estimate forward without waiting for the original, slow pipeline to catch up.

en.caption: Figure 1. End-to-end overview of CMO-NRT. Left: the five methodological steps, from cleaning and aligning data, cutting it into patches, and training a CNN with semi-supervised learning, to K-fold ensembling and prediction. Right: the setup details, showing the observable features (year, month, latitude, longitude, and nine environmental variables) that the model uses to reproduce each of the ten GOBMs and eight data products on the global 180x360 grid.

en.text: The method: learn the models, then run ahead of them

The predictors are deliberately mundane and, crucially, timely: year, month, latitude, longitude, and nine environmental variables such as sea-surface temperature (SST), sea ice (ICE), chlorophyll (CHL), mixed-layer depth (MLD), atmospheric CO2, salinity (SSS), sea-surface height (SSH), sea-level pressure (SLP), and wind. The global 180x360 grid is cut into small 18x18 patches and fed through a stack of convolutional layers followed by linear layers, which map the nine input channels through hidden widths of 64 down to a single predicted value per grid cell.

The interesting part is how the model is trained. Labeled grid cells give a standard supervised error, but observations are sparse, so the authors add a semi-supervised term. The same patch is shown to the network twice, once weakly augmented with 10% of its features masked and once strongly augmented with 30% masked, and an unsupervised consistency loss penalizes any disagreement between the two predictions. Combining a supervised RMSE loss with this consistency loss (the total is L = w*L_u + L_s) makes the model noticeably more stable where labels run out.

en.caption: Figure 2. The semi-supervised training scheme. Labeled patches feed a supervised RMSE loss (L_s), while the same unlabeled patches are passed through weak (10% masked) and strong (30% masked) augmentations, and the disagreement between the two predictions forms the unsupervised consistency loss (L_u). The two are combined as L = w*L_u + L_s. Inset: the CNN-plus-linear model structure, stacking 18x18 patches through convolutional and linear layers.

en.text: Two more engineering details make the system usable in practice. Predictions are ensembled through K-fold cross-validation to reduce variance, and because one key input, atmospheric CO2 (xCO2), is itself only available up to the end of 2022, the authors train a separate small model to extend xCO2 to the present. That auxiliary model reaches a test RMSE of 1.74, about a 0.5% error, which is accurate enough to feed the main pipeline without introducing meaningful drift.
What it produces: the sink, extended to the present month

The payoff is a dataset that carries the ocean carbon record past where the Global Carbon Budget stops. Applying the framework to all ten GOBMs and eight data products of the Global Carbon Budget 2022 yields monthly, gridded maps of surface-ocean fCO2 and air-sea CO2 flux running from January 2022 through July 2023, seamlessly continuing the historical series.

en.caption: Figure 3. CMO-NRT extends the record to near-real-time. In the fCO2 (A) and air-sea CO2 flux (B) time series, the black line is the 1990-2021 Global Carbon Budget 2022 estimate and the red line is the CMO-NRT near-real-time prediction through July 2023, picking up smoothly where the historical record ends; grey shading spans the range across the ten GOBMs and eight data products. Panels C and D map the mean fCO2 and flux over August 2022-July 2023.

en.text: The red segment in panels A and B is the whole point: it is the part of the curve that, until now, would not have existed for another year. The gridded maps in C and D show that the near-real-time product is not just a global number but a spatially resolved field, with the familiar pattern of CO2 outgassing in the equatorial Pacific and uptake in the higher-latitude oceans.
Does it faithfully reproduce the originals?

A near-real-time estimate is only useful if it matches what the trusted models would have said. To test this honestly, the authors held out the most recent two years of every model and product, trained only on earlier data, and then predicted the withheld 2020-2021 period so it could be compared against the known originals.

en.caption: Figure 5. Gridded agreement between CMO-NRT predictions and the original outputs for each of the ten GOBMs over 2020-2021. Points cluster tightly along the 1:1 line (grey), with the total-least-squares fit (red) nearly coincident; per-model correlations run from R² = 0.87 to 0.97, most above 0.9.

en.text: For the biogeochemical models the agreement is strong and consistent: the ten GOBMs land between R² = 0.87 and 0.97, with several, such as MRI-ESM2-1 (0.97) and CESM2 (0.96), reproduced almost exactly. The table below lists the full set.

en.caption: Table 1. Gridded correlation (R²) between CMO-NRT predictions and the original outputs for each of the ten GOBMs over the held-out 2020-2021 period (from Figure 5).

en.text: The data products are the harder case, and the paper does not hide it. Compared model-by-model on global monthly averages, some products are reproduced beautifully (NIES-NN and OSETHZ-GRaCER both reach R² = 0.98, UOEX-Watson 0.96), while others are noticeably noisier, with occasional points scattering away from the fit line (Jena-MLS at 0.65 and MPI-SOMFFN at 0.53 are the weakest).

en.caption: Figure 8. Global-average monthly fCO2 for each of the eight data products over 2020-2021: original values (black), CMO-NRT predictions (red), and the mean across all products (dashed grey). Agreement is excellent for products like NIES-NN and OSETHZ-GRaCER (R² = 0.98) but weaker for MPI-SOMFFN (R² = 0.53), reflecting the larger internal variability of some data products.

en.text: Across the global monthly aggregates the predictions run only slightly high, with most differences under 3 uatm, and the aggregate correlations stay mostly above R² = 0.85. In short, the framework tracks the GOBMs almost perfectly and the stronger data products very well, while remaining candid about the handful of products that are genuinely harder to reproduce.
Where the residuals live

Beyond global averages, it matters whether the small remaining errors are spread evenly or concentrated in a few regions that could bias a basin-scale budget. Mapping the prediction-minus-original differences month by month shows that agreement is broadly uniform across the globe.

en.caption: Figure 11. Spatial differences between CMO-NRT predictions and the ten-GOBM average across the twelve months of 2020-2021; side panels show the zonal (latitude) profiles. Residuals are small and largely uniform, with the largest discrepancies concentrated in the Arctic Ocean and the equatorial Pacific.

en.text: The maps are mostly pale, meaning small residuals nearly everywhere. What structure remains is concentrated where it is physically hardest to model: the Arctic Ocean, where sea-ice cover and sparse observations complicate the surface CO2 field, and the equatorial Pacific, where strong upwelling drives large CO2 gradients. These are exactly the regions to treat with caution when reading the near-real-time product.
Why it matters

CMO-NRT does not reinvent ocean carbon science; it makes the existing, trusted science timely. By pairing convolutional networks with semi-supervised learning to update ten GOBMs and eight data products, it turns a picture of the global ocean carbon sink that used to arrive a year late into a near-real-time, monthly, gridded monitor, here covering January 2022 through July 2023.

For the scientists and policymakers working through the global stocktake, that is the difference between reacting to last year's ocean and watching this year's. The honest boundaries are stated plainly: a couple of noisier data products, and residuals that concentrate in the Arctic and equatorial Pacific. With the dataset and code released openly on Figshare and the project website, the more valuable contribution may be the template itself, a reusable recipe for pulling slow, model-based climate indicators up to the present month.

zh.text: 海洋是地球对抗气候变化最大的缓冲器之一，每年吸收人类排放二氧化碳的约四分之一。但我们对“海洋到底吸收了多少”的官方核算，也就是每年发布的全球碳收支（Global Carbon Budget），总是滞后现实大约一年。等到海洋的吸收能力发生变化时，我们往往要在很久之后才能察觉。
这种滞后并非疏忽，而是被“写死”在数据的生产方式里。用来估算碳汇的海洋生物地球化学模型（GOBM）计算量极大；而数据驱动型产品所依赖的表层海洋二氧化碳观测，本身也要延迟约一年。于是学界手里有一批细致、可信的海洋碳通量数据库，却始终在“回望过去”。
偏偏在最需要及时信息的当下，这个空档格外尴尬。随着各国推进《巴黎协定》下的全球盘点（global stocktake），它们需要知道碳“现在”去了哪里，而不是一年前。本文的贡献正是补上这段空档：Carbon Monitor Ocean（简称 CMO-NRT），一套近实时、按月、网格化的全球表层海洋二氧化碳逸度（fCO2）与海气二氧化碳通量数据集，以及生成它的深度学习框架。
相关链接
论文：https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.01637
代码：https://github.com/kepiyu/CMO-NRT
数据集（Figshare）：https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.24658494.v1 ｜ 在线项目：https://carbonsink.microsoft.com/
这里最关键的设计，是 CMO-NRT “不做什么”：它不去替换这些被广泛信任的社区模型，而是学着用近实时可得的输入把它们复现出来。每一个 GOBM 或数据产品都被当作一个“目标”，神经网络学习从可观测量预测它。这样一来，只要当月的观测数据到位，模型就能把估计向前延伸，而不必等待原本缓慢的计算流程追上。

zh.caption: 图1 CMO-NRT 的整体流程。左侧是方法的五个步骤：清洗与对齐数据、切分为小块、用半监督学习训练 CNN、K 折集成，最后给出预测。右侧是具体设置：模型仅用可观测特征（年、月、纬度、经度以及九个环境变量），在全球 180x360 网格上复现十个 GOBM 与八种数据产品的输出。

zh.text: 方法：先学会模型，再跑在它们前面

所用的预测变量都很朴素，但关键在于“及时”：年、月、纬度、经度，以及九个环境变量，例如海表温度（SST）、海冰（ICE）、叶绿素（CHL）、混合层深度（MLD）、大气二氧化碳（CO2）、盐度（SSS）、海表高度（SSH）、海平面气压（SLP）和风（Wind）。全球 180x360 的网格被切成一个个 18x18 的小块，送入若干卷积层再接线性层：把九个输入通道经由 64 维的隐藏宽度，逐格映射到一个预测值。
真正有意思的是训练方式。有标注的网格点提供常规的监督误差，但观测本就稀疏，于是作者加入了一个半监督项。同一个小块会被送入网络两次：一次是弱增强（遮蔽 10% 特征），一次是强增强（遮蔽 30% 特征），一个无监督一致性损失会惩罚两次预测之间的不一致。把监督 RMSE 损失与这一致性损失相加（总损失 L = w·L_u + L_s），能让模型在缺少标注的地方明显更稳。

zh.caption: 图2 半监督训练方案。有标注的小块进入监督 RMSE 损失（L_s）；同一批无标注小块分别经过弱增强（遮蔽 10%）与强增强（遮蔽 30%），两次预测之间的差异构成无监督一致性损失（L_u）。二者合并为 L = w·L_u + L_s。右下角为 CNN 加线性层的模型结构，将 18x18 的小块逐层处理。

zh.text: 还有两处工程细节让系统真正可用。预测通过 K 折交叉验证做集成以降低方差；另外，由于一个关键输入，即大气二氧化碳（xCO2）本身只更新到 2022 年底，作者单独训练了一个小模型把 xCO2 延伸到当下。这个辅助模型的测试 RMSE 为 1.74，约合 0.5% 的误差，足够精确，能在不引入明显漂移的前提下喂给主流程。
它产出了什么：把碳汇延伸到当月
回报是一套把海洋碳记录接续到全球碳收支“断点”之后的数据集。将该框架应用到全球碳收支 2022（Global Carbon Budget 2022）中全部十个 GOBM 与八种数据产品，就得到按月、网格化的表层海洋 fCO2 与海气二氧化碳通量图，时间跨度从 2022 年一月延续到 2023 年七月，与历史序列平滑衔接。
下面这张图把整套框架的产出画在了一起，值得先说清楚怎么看：上半部分是两条随时间变化的曲线，分别对应全球平均的海洋二氧化碳逸度与海气通量；下半部分则是两幅世界地图，给出某一时段各海域的空间分布。真正的看点在曲线的最右端，也就是那截与历史记录平滑接续、此前需要再等一年才会出现的新曲线。读图时，不妨把黑线看作过去、把红线看作被补上的当下；地图上的深浅则对应各处二氧化碳逸度与通量的高低。

zh.caption: 图3 CMO-NRT 把记录延伸到近实时。在 fCO2（A）与海气二氧化碳通量（B）的时间序列中，黑线是 1990–2021 年全球碳收支 2022 的估计，红线是 CMO-NRT 直到 2023 年七月的近实时预测，恰好从历史记录的末端平滑接起；灰色阴影表示十个 GOBM 与八种数据产品的范围。C、D 两图给出 2022 年八月至 2023 年七月的平均 fCO2 与通量分布。

zh.text: A、B 两图中的那段红线才是重点：它正是那段“若按老办法还要再等一年才会出现”的曲线。C、D 的网格图说明，这个近实时产品不只是一个全球数字，而是一个有空间分辨率的场：赤道太平洋一带二氧化碳向外释放、较高纬度海域则以吸收为主，都是我们熟悉的格局。
它复现原始结果够不够忠实？
一个近实时估计只有在能与可信模型“本会给出的结果”对上时才有意义。为了诚实地检验这一点，作者把每个模型和产品最近两年的数据留出，只用更早的数据训练，再去预测被留出的 2020–2021 年，以便与已知的原始结果对照。

zh.caption: 图5 2020–2021 年间，CMO-NRT 预测与十个 GOBM 各自原始输出之间的逐格一致性。散点紧贴 1:1 灰线，红色的总体最小二乘拟合线几乎与之重合；各模型相关性从 R² = 0.87 到 0.97，多数高于 0.9。

zh.text: 对生物地球化学模型来说，这种一致性既强又稳：十个 GOBM 的 R² 介于 0.87 到 0.97 之间，其中若干个，例如 MRI-ESM2-1（0.97）与 CESM2（0.96），几乎被完全复现。下表列出完整结果。

zh.caption: 表1 留出的 2020–2021 年间，CMO-NRT 预测与十个 GOBM 各自原始输出之间的逐格相关性 R²（对应图5）。
headers: 海洋生物地球化学模型（GOBM）

zh.text: 数据产品是更难的一类，本文也没有回避。在全球逐月平均上逐个对比时，有些产品被复现得很漂亮（NIES-NN 与 OSETHZ-GRaCER 都达到 R² = 0.98，UOEX-Watson 为 0.96），另一些则明显更“吵”，个别点会偏离拟合线，其中 Jena-MLS（0.65）与 MPI-SOMFFN（0.53）表现最弱，代表了本框架较难忠实复现的一类产品。

zh.caption: 图8 2020–2021 年间，八种数据产品各自的全球逐月平均 fCO2：原始值（黑）、CMO-NRT 预测（红）与所有产品的均值（灰色虚线）。对 NIES-NN、OSETHZ-GRaCER 这类产品吻合极佳（R² = 0.98），对 MPI-SOMFFN 则较弱（R² = 0.53），反映出部分数据产品自身波动更大。

zh.text: 在全球逐月的聚合量上，预测值只是略高，多数差异小于 3 µatm，聚合相关性也多数高于 R² = 0.85。一句话：这套框架几乎完美地跟住了 GOBM，对表现较好的数据产品也很贴合，同时对那些更难复现的产品保持透明。
残差落在哪里
除了全球平均，还要看剩下的小误差是均匀铺开，还是集中在少数几个可能扭曲海盆尺度收支的区域。把“预测减原始”的差异逐月成图后可以看到，一致性在全球范围内大体是均匀的。

zh.caption: 图11 2020–2021 十二个月里，CMO-NRT 预测与十个 GOBM 平均之间的空间差异；两侧小图给出随纬度变化的经向廓线。残差普遍很小且大体均匀，最大的差异集中在北冰洋与赤道太平洋。

zh.text: 这些图大多是浅色的，意味着几乎处处残差都很小。仅存的结构，恰恰集中在物理上最难建模的地方：北冰洋，那里海冰覆盖与观测稀疏让表层二氧化碳场变得复杂；以及赤道太平洋，强烈的上升流带来很大的二氧化碳梯度。读近实时产品时，这两个区域正是需要格外谨慎的地方。
为什么重要
CMO-NRT 并没有重写海洋碳科学，而是让既有的、可信的科学变得及时。通过把卷积网络与半监督学习结合起来更新十个 GOBM 与八种数据产品，它把一幅过去总要迟到一年的全球海洋碳汇图像，变成了近实时、按月、网格化的监测，这里覆盖 2022 年一月到 2023 年七月。
对正在推进全球盘点的科研人员和决策者来说，这就是“对着去年的海洋做反应”与“看着今年的海洋”之间的区别。文章也把边界讲得很清楚：少数几个更“吵”的数据产品，以及集中在北冰洋和赤道太平洋的残差。随着数据集与代码在 Figshare 和项目网站上公开，或许更有价值的贡献是这套模板本身：一份把缓慢的、基于模型的气候指标拉到当月的可复用配方。

en.title: From a Year Behind to Near-Real-Time: Watching the Ocean Carbon Sink as It Happens
en.subtitle: Carbon Monitor Ocean (CMO-NRT) uses CNNs and semi-supervised learning to update ten ocean biogeochemical models and eight data products to the present month. From Tsinghua University, Microsoft Research, the University of Exeter and collaborators.

zh.title: 从滞后一年到近实时：把海洋碳汇的变化“看在当下”

en.text: The ocean is one of the planet's largest buffers against climate change, soaking up roughly a quarter of the carbon dioxide humanity emits every year. This is an awkward gap at exactly the wrong moment. As countries move through the global stocktake under the Paris Agreement, they need to know where the carbon is going now, not a year ago. zh.caption: 图1 CMO-NRT 的整体流程。左侧是方法的五个步骤：清洗与对齐数据、切分为小块、用半监督学习训练 CNN、K 折集成，最后给出预测。右侧是具体设置：模型仅用可观测特征（年、月、纬度、经度以及九个环境变量），在全球 180x360 网格上复现十个 GOBM 与八种数据产品的输出。

zh.text: 为什么重要
CMO-NRT 并没有重写海洋碳科学，而是让既有的、可信的科学变得及时。通过把卷积网络与半监督学习结合起来更新十个 GOBM 与八种数据产品，它把一幅过去总要迟到一年的全球海洋碳汇图像，变成了近实时、按月、网格化的监测，这里覆盖 2022 年一月到 2023 年七月。
对正在推进全球盘点的科研人员和决策者来说，这就是“对着去年的海洋做反应”与“看着今年的海洋”之间的区别。文章也把边界讲得很清楚：少数几个更“吵”的数据产品，以及集中在北冰洋和赤道太平洋的残差。随着数据集与代码在 Figshare 和项目网站上公开，或许更有价值的贡献是这套模板本身：一份把缓慢的、基于模型的气候指标拉到当月的可复用配方。

zh.subtitle: Carbon Monitor Ocean（CMO-NRT）用 CNN 与半监督学习，把十个海洋生物地球化学模型和八种数据产品更新到当月。来自清华大学、微软研究院、埃克塞特大学（University of Exeter）等机构。

en.text: Links
Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.01637
Code: https://github.com/kepiyu/CMO-NRT
Dataset (Figshare): https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.24658494.v1 | Live project: https://carbonsink.microsoft.com/

The key design choice is what CMO-NRT does not do: it does not try to replace the trusted community models. Instead it learns to reproduce them from inputs that are available in near-real-time. Each GOBM or data product becomes a target that a neural network learns to predict from observable quantities, so that once those observables arrive for the current month, the model can extend the estimate forward without waiting for the original, slow pipeline to catch up.

en.caption: Figure 1. End-to-end overview of CMO-NRT. Left: the five methodological steps, from cleaning and aligning data, cutting it into patches, and training a CNN with semi-supervised learning, to K-fold ensembling and prediction. Right: the setup details, showing the observable features (year, month, latitude, longitude, and nine environmental variables) that the model uses to reproduce each of the ten GOBMs and eight data products on the global 180x360 grid.

en.text: The method: learn the models, then run ahead of them

The predictors are deliberately mundane and, crucially, timely: year, month, latitude, longitude, and nine environmental variables such as sea-surface temperature (SST), sea ice (ICE), chlorophyll (CHL), mixed-layer depth (MLD), atmospheric CO2, salinity (SSS), sea-surface height (SSH), sea-level pressure (SLP), and wind. The global 180x360 grid is cut into small 18x18 patches and fed through a stack of convolutional layers followed by linear layers, which map the nine input channels through hidden widths of 64 down to a single predicted value per grid cell.

The interesting part is how the model is trained. Labeled grid cells give a standard supervised error, but observations are sparse, so the authors add a semi-supervised term. The same patch is shown to the network twice, once weakly augmented with 10% of its features masked and once strongly augmented with 30% masked, and an unsupervised consistency loss penalizes any disagreement between the two predictions. Combining a supervised RMSE loss with this consistency loss (the total is L = w*L_u + L_s) makes the model noticeably more stable where labels run out.

en.caption: Figure 2. The semi-supervised training scheme. Labeled patches feed a supervised RMSE loss (L_s), while the same unlabeled patches are passed through weak (10% masked) and strong (30% masked) augmentations, and the disagreement between the two predictions forms the unsupervised consistency loss (L_u). The two are combined as L = w*L_u + L_s. Inset: the CNN-plus-linear model structure, stacking 18x18 patches through convolutional and linear layers.

en.text: Two more engineering details make the system usable in practice. Predictions are ensembled through K-fold cross-validation to reduce variance, and because one key input, atmospheric CO2 (xCO2), is itself only available up to the end of 2022, the authors train a separate small model to extend xCO2 to the present. That auxiliary model reaches a test RMSE of 1.74, about a 0.5% error, which is accurate enough to feed the main pipeline without introducing meaningful drift.

zh.caption: 图1 CMO-NRT 的整体流程。左侧是方法的五个步骤：清洗与对齐数据、切分为小块、用半监督学习训练 CNN、K 折集成，最后给出预测。右侧是具体设置：模型仅用可观测特征（年、月、纬度、经度以及九个环境变量），在全球 180x360 网格上复现十个 GOBM 与八种数据产品的输出。

zh.text: 方法：先学会模型，再跑在它们前面

所用的预测变量都很朴素，但关键在于“及时”：年、月、纬度、经度，以及九个环境变量，例如海表温度（SST）、海冰（ICE）、叶绿素（CHL）、混合层深度（MLD）、大气二氧化碳（CO2）、盐度（SSS）、海表高度（SSH）、海平面气压（SLP）和风（Wind）。全球 180x360 的网格被切成一个个 18x18 的小块，送入若干卷积层再接线性层：把九个输入通道经由 64 维的隐藏宽度，逐格映射到一个预测值。
真正有意思的是训练方式。有标注的网格点提供常规的监督误差，但观测本就稀疏，于是作者加入了一个半监督项。同一个小块会被送入网络两次：一次是弱增强（遮蔽 10% 特征），一次是强增强（遮蔽 30% 特征），一个无监督一致性损失会惩罚两次预测之间的不一致。把监督 RMSE 损失与这一致性损失相加（总损失 L = w·L_u + L_s），能让模型在缺少标注的地方明显更稳。

zh.caption: 图2 半监督训练方案。有标注的小块进入监督 RMSE 损失（L_s）；同一批无标注小块分别经过弱增强（遮蔽 10%）与强增强（遮蔽 30%），两次预测之间的差异构成无监督一致性损失（L_u）。二者合并为 L = w·L_u + L_s。右下角为 CNN 加线性层的模型结构，将 18x18 的小块逐层处理。

zh.text: 还有两处工程细节让系统真正可用。预测通过 K 折交叉验证做集成以降低方差；另外，由于一个关键输入，即大气二氧化碳（xCO2）本身只更新到 2022 年底，作者单独训练了一个小模型把 xCO2 延伸到当下。这个辅助模型的测试 RMSE 为 1.74，约合 0.5% 的误差，足够精确，能在不引入明显漂移的前提下喂给主流程。

zh.subtitle: Carbon Monitor Ocean（CMO-NRT）用 CNN 与半监督学习，把十个海洋生物地球化学模型和八种数据产品更新到当月。来自清华大学、微软研究院、埃克塞特大学（University of Exeter）等机构。

en.text: The ocean is one of the planet's largest buffers against climate change, soaking up roughly a quarter of the carbon dioxide humanity emits every year. Yet our best official accounting of how much it absorbs, the annual Global Carbon Budget, always trails reality by about a year. When the ocean's uptake shifts, we cannot see it until long after the fact.

That lag is not an oversight; it is built into how the number is produced. The ocean biogeochemical models (GOBMs) that estimate the sink are computationally heavy, and the surface-ocean CO2 observations that data-driven products depend on are themselves delayed by roughly a year. So the community has detailed, trustworthy databases of ocean carbon fluxes that are always looking backward in time.

Does it faithfully reproduce the originals?

A near-real-time estimate is only useful if it matches what the trusted models would have said. To test this honestly, the authors held out the most recent two years of every model and product, trained only on earlier data, and then predicted the withheld 2020-2021 period so it could be compared against the known originals.

en.caption: Figure 5. Gridded agreement between CMO-NRT predictions and the original outputs for each of the ten GOBMs over 2020-2021. Points cluster tightly along the 1:1 line (grey), with the total-least-squares fit (red) nearly coincident; per-model correlations run from R² = 0.87 to 0.97, most above 0.9.

en.text: For the biogeochemical models the agreement is strong and consistent: the ten GOBMs land between R² = 0.87 and 0.97, with several, such as MRI-ESM2-1 (0.97) and CESM2 (0.96), reproduced almost exactly. The table below lists the full set.

en.caption: Table 1. Gridded correlation (R²) between CMO-NRT predictions and the original outputs for each of the ten GOBMs over the held-out 2020-2021 period (from Figure 5).

en.text: The data products are the harder case, and the paper does not hide it. Compared model-by-model on global monthly averages, some products are reproduced beautifully (NIES-NN and OSETHZ-GRaCER both reach R² = 0.98, UOEX-Watson 0.96), while others are noticeably noisier, with occasional points scattering away from the fit line (Jena-MLS at 0.65 and MPI-SOMFFN at 0.53 are the weakest).

en.caption: Figure 8. Global-average monthly fCO2 for each of the eight data products over 2020-2021: original values (black), CMO-NRT predictions (red), and the mean across all products (dashed grey). Agreement is excellent for products like NIES-NN and OSETHZ-GRaCER (R² = 0.98) but weaker for MPI-SOMFFN (R² = 0.53), reflecting the larger internal variability of some data products.

en.text: Across the global monthly aggregates the predictions run only slightly high, with most differences under 3 uatm, and the aggregate correlations stay mostly above R² = 0.85. In short, the framework tracks the GOBMs almost perfectly and the stronger data products very well, while remaining candid about the handful of products that are genuinely harder to reproduce.

zh.text: 它复现原始结果够不够忠实？
一个近实时估计只有在能与可信模型“本会给出的结果”对上时才有意义。为了诚实地检验这一点，作者把每个模型和产品最近两年的数据留出，只用更早的数据训练，再去预测被留出的 2020–2021 年，以便与已知的原始结果对照。

zh.caption: 图5 2020–2021 年间，CMO-NRT 预测与十个 GOBM 各自原始输出之间的逐格一致性。散点紧贴 1:1 灰线，红色的总体最小二乘拟合线几乎与之重合；各模型相关性从 R² = 0.87 到 0.97，多数高于 0.9。

zh.text: 对生物地球化学模型来说，这种一致性既强又稳：十个 GOBM 的 R² 介于 0.87 到 0.97 之间，其中若干个，例如 MRI-ESM2-1（0.97）与 CESM2（0.96），几乎被完全复现。下表列出完整结果。

zh.caption: 表1 留出的 2020–2021 年间，CMO-NRT 预测与十个 GOBM 各自原始输出之间的逐格相关性 R²（对应图5）。
headers: 海洋生物地球化学模型（GOBM）

zh.text: 数据产品是更难的一类，本文也没有回避。在全球逐月平均上逐个对比时，有些产品被复现得很漂亮（NIES-NN 与 OSETHZ-GRaCER 都达到 R² = 0.98，UOEX-Watson 为 0.96），另一些则明显更“吵”，个别点会偏离拟合线，其中 Jena-MLS（0.65）与 MPI-SOMFFN（0.53）表现最弱，代表了本框架较难忠实复现的一类产品。

zh.caption: 图8 2020–2021 年间，八种数据产品各自的全球逐月平均 fCO2：原始值（黑）、CMO-NRT 预测（红）与所有产品的均值（灰色虚线）。对 NIES-NN、OSETHZ-GRaCER 这类产品吻合极佳（R² = 0.98），对 MPI-SOMFFN 则较弱（R² = 0.53），反映出部分数据产品自身波动更大。

zh.text: 在全球逐月的聚合量上，预测值只是略高，多数差异小于 3 µatm，聚合相关性也多数高于 R² = 0.85。一句话：这套框架几乎完美地跟住了 GOBM，对表现较好的数据产品也很贴合，同时对那些更难复现的产品保持透明。

en.title: From a Year Behind to Near-Real-Time: Watching the Ocean Carbon Sink as It Happens
en.subtitle: Carbon Monitor Ocean (CMO-NRT) uses CNNs and semi-supervised learning to update ten ocean biogeochemical models and eight data products to the present month. From Tsinghua University, Microsoft Research, the University of Exeter and collaborators.

zh.title: 从滞后一年到近实时：把海洋碳汇的变化“看在当下”
zh.subtitle: Carbon Monitor Ocean（CMO-NRT）用 CNN 与半监督学习，把十个海洋生物地球化学模型和八种数据产品更新到当月。来自清华大学、微软研究院、埃克塞特大学（University of Exeter）等机构。

en.text: Where the residuals live

Beyond global averages, it matters whether the small remaining errors are spread evenly or concentrated in a few regions that could bias a basin-scale budget. Mapping the prediction-minus-original differences month by month shows that agreement is broadly uniform across the globe.

en.caption: Figure 11. Spatial differences between CMO-NRT predictions and the ten-GOBM average across the twelve months of 2020-2021; side panels show the zonal (latitude) profiles. Residuals are small and largely uniform, with the largest discrepancies concentrated in the Arctic Ocean and the equatorial Pacific.

en.text: The maps are mostly pale, meaning small residuals nearly everywhere. What structure remains is concentrated where it is physically hardest to model: the Arctic Ocean, where sea-ice cover and sparse observations complicate the surface CO2 field, and the equatorial Pacific, where strong upwelling drives large CO2 gradients. These are exactly the regions to treat with caution when reading the near-real-time product.

zh.text: 残差落在哪里
除了全球平均，还要看剩下的小误差是均匀铺开，还是集中在少数几个可能扭曲海盆尺度收支的区域。把“预测减原始”的差异逐月成图后可以看到，一致性在全球范围内大体是均匀的。

zh.caption: 图11 2020–2021 十二个月里，CMO-NRT 预测与十个 GOBM 平均之间的空间差异；两侧小图给出随纬度变化的经向廓线。残差普遍很小且大体均匀，最大的差异集中在北冰洋与赤道太平洋。

zh.text: 这些图大多是浅色的，意味着几乎处处残差都很小。仅存的结构，恰恰集中在物理上最难建模的地方：北冰洋，那里海冰覆盖与观测稀疏让表层二氧化碳场变得复杂；以及赤道太平洋，强烈的上升流带来很大的二氧化碳梯度。读近实时产品时，这两个区域正是需要格外谨慎的地方。

en.title: From a Year Behind to Near-Real-Time: Watching the Ocean Carbon Sink as It Happens
en.subtitle: Carbon Monitor Ocean (CMO-NRT) uses CNNs and semi-supervised learning to update ten ocean biogeochemical models and eight data products to the present month. From Tsinghua University, Microsoft Research, the University of Exeter and collaborators.

zh.title: 从滞后一年到近实时：把海洋碳汇的变化“看在当下”
zh.subtitle: Carbon Monitor Ocean（CMO-NRT）用 CNN 与半监督学习，把十个海洋生物地球化学模型和八种数据产品更新到当月。来自清华大学、微软研究院、埃克塞特大学（University of Exeter）等机构。

en.text: The method: learn the models, then run ahead of them

The predictors are deliberately mundane and, crucially, timely: year, month, latitude, longitude, and nine environmental variables such as sea-surface temperature (SST), sea ice (ICE), chlorophyll (CHL), mixed-layer depth (MLD), atmospheric CO2, salinity (SSS), sea-surface height (SSH), sea-level pressure (SLP), and wind. The global 180x360 grid is cut into small 18x18 patches and fed through a stack of convolutional layers followed by linear layers, which map the nine input channels through hidden widths of 64 down to a single predicted value per grid cell.

The interesting part is how the model is trained. Labeled grid cells give a standard supervised error, but observations are sparse, so the authors add a semi-supervised term. The same patch is shown to the network twice, once weakly augmented with 10% of its features masked and once strongly augmented with 30% masked, and an unsupervised consistency loss penalizes any disagreement between the two predictions. Combining a supervised RMSE loss with this consistency loss (the total is L = w*L_u + L_s) makes the model noticeably more stable where labels run out.

en.caption: Figure 2. The semi-supervised training scheme. Labeled patches feed a supervised RMSE loss (L_s), while the same unlabeled patches are passed through weak (10% masked) and strong (30% masked) augmentations, and the disagreement between the two predictions forms the unsupervised consistency loss (L_u). The two are combined as L = w*L_u + L_s. Inset: the CNN-plus-linear model structure, stacking 18x18 patches through convolutional and linear layers.

en.text: Two more engineering details make the system usable in practice. Predictions are ensembled through K-fold cross-validation to reduce variance, and because one key input, atmospheric CO2 (xCO2), is itself only available up to the end of 2022, the authors train a separate small model to extend xCO2 to the present. That auxiliary model reaches a test RMSE of 1.74, about a 0.5% error, which is accurate enough to feed the main pipeline without introducing meaningful drift.

zh.text: 它产出了什么：把碳汇延伸到当月
回报是一套把海洋碳记录接续到全球碳收支“断点”之后的数据集。将该框架应用到全球碳收支 2022（Global Carbon Budget 2022）中全部十个 GOBM 与八种数据产品，就得到按月、网格化的表层海洋 fCO2 与海气二氧化碳通量图，时间跨度从 2022 年一月延续到 2023 年七月，与历史序列平滑衔接。
下面这张图把整套框架的产出画在了一起，值得先说清楚怎么看：上半部分是两条随时间变化的曲线，分别对应全球平均的海洋二氧化碳逸度与海气通量；下半部分则是两幅世界地图，给出某一时段各海域的空间分布。真正的看点在曲线的最右端，也就是那截与历史记录平滑接续、此前需要再等一年才会出现的新曲线。读图时，不妨把黑线看作过去、把红线看作被补上的当下；地图上的深浅则对应各处二氧化碳逸度与通量的高低。

zh.caption: 图3 CMO-NRT 把记录延伸到近实时。在 fCO2（A）与海气二氧化碳通量（B）的时间序列中，黑线是 1990–2021 年全球碳收支 2022 的估计，红线是 CMO-NRT 直到 2023 年七月的近实时预测，恰好从历史记录的末端平滑接起；灰色阴影表示十个 GOBM 与八种数据产品的范围。C、D 两图给出 2022 年八月至 2023 年七月的平均 fCO2 与通量分布。

zh.text: A、B 两图中的那段红线才是重点：它正是那段“若按老办法还要再等一年才会出现”的曲线。C、D 的网格图说明，这个近实时产品不只是一个全球数字，而是一个有空间分辨率的场：赤道太平洋一带二氧化碳向外释放、较高纬度海域则以吸收为主，都是我们熟悉的格局。

zh.caption: 图1 CMO-NRT 的整体流程。左侧是方法的五个步骤：清洗与对齐数据、切分为小块、用半监督学习训练 CNN、K 折集成，最后给出预测。右侧是具体设置：模型仅用可观测特征（年、月、纬度、经度以及九个环境变量），在全球 180x360 网格上复现十个 GOBM 与八种数据产品的输出。

zh.text: 为什么重要
CMO-NRT 并没有重写海洋碳科学，而是让既有的、可信的科学变得及时。通过把卷积网络与半监督学习结合起来更新十个 GOBM 与八种数据产品，它把一幅过去总要迟到一年的全球海洋碳汇图像，变成了近实时、按月、网格化的监测，这里覆盖 2022 年一月到 2023 年七月。
对正在推进全球盘点的科研人员和决策者来说，这就是“对着去年的海洋做反应”与“看着今年的海洋”之间的区别。文章也把边界讲得很清楚：少数几个更“吵”的数据产品，以及集中在北冰洋和赤道太平洋的残差。随着数据集与代码在 Figshare 和项目网站上公开，或许更有价值的贡献是这套模板本身：一份把缓慢的、基于模型的气候指标拉到当月的可复用配方。
